status: pass conditional numerical thresholds, subject to boundary tolerance
proof: With nonnegative weights increasing Zurich utility increases its lower score monotonically; upper scores are fixed. Its exclusive regret falls, all other city regrets stay fixed, so its gap against the best other action is nonincreasing and a strict sign-changing crossing is unique where the score is strictly increasing. Another city remains possible exactly while its upper score is at least the greatest competing lower score; only the Zurich lower score moves. The independently enumerated sign crossings identify all interior boundaries. Exact observed identification would change upper as well as lower and is not covered.
boundary_caveat: Mathematical equality admits ties; interval_decision uses 1e-12 score tolerance for possible/necessary status while decision_rank uses exact floating-point regret ranks. Thus at or extremely near a root rank output can pick one side due to rounding and strict exclusion occurs only past the implemented tolerance; below/above 1e-6 probes are not a certificate of bit-exact boundary classification.
scope: Conditional sensitivity targets only, not observed data, actual acquisition, a forecast, or a primary update. 63925 is canton pupils and is not an admitted city pupil upper bound; FTE conversion requires verified stage/provider/geography/date matching and a valid target pupil upper bound, plus a lower bound on matching teaching activity. Travel utility target does not determine a mean, trip distribution, or school population. No upstream scientific validity audit; source hash checks establish only file identity.
